claims.statement: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 requires a battery passport from 18 February 2027 for LMT batteries, EV batteries, and industrial batteries above 2 kWh.

The passport must combine model and individual-battery information, use a QR-linked unique identifier, support differentiated access, and remain accurate, complete, and current under the responsible operator.

contrary_evidence: The regulation leaves technical detail to standards and implementing acts, so an early implementation can require rework.
Large manufacturers and ERP vendors may build the passport layer internally.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a growing exception corpus and reusable mappings from messy supplier BOMs to passport fields
fingerprint.customer: independent EU industrial-battery and light-mobility battery assemblers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: embedded referrals and connectors through battery ERP vendors, test laboratories, and conformity advisers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: managed passport data plane with schema validation, role-based disclosure, immutable change history, and hosted QR resolution
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the economic operator pays on onboarding, monthly access, and each serial passport activation
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a model, serial unit, component revision, ownership status, or state-of-health datum must enter or update a legally required passport

founder_fit: Strong fit with data engineering, AI-assisted schema mapping, EU context, and the family renewable-energy channel; it is asynchronous, capital-light, and can begin with one battery category.
risks: Incorrect passport data could create market-surveillance and contractual liability.
Supplier confidentiality makes access control and data minimisation essential.
The product must not represent itself as a notified body or legal certification.

structure.control_point: the validated passport record and QR resolver used before an eligible battery is placed on the EU market
structure.critical_dependency: permissioned component, conformity, carbon, and lifecycle data from the maker and its upstream suppliers

thesis: A narrow data plane can turn component, conformity, carbon-footprint, and in-use records into permissioned, updateable battery passports for independent industrial-battery assemblers that cannot justify an internal platform. The recurring trigger is every model release, serialised unit, component change, and state-of-health update; ERP and conformity-assessment partners can distribute it one-to-many.
title: Battery Passport Integrity Plane for Independent EU Pack Makers
uncertainties: Whether independent pack makers will buy a standalone layer rather than an ERP module.
Actual serial volumes and willingness to pay.
Final interoperability standards and identity architecture.
